jobs.title: Director, Digital Product Operations & Strategy
jobs.description:
The Director, Digital Product Operations & Strategy is accountable for building and continuously improving the operating as well as enablement system that empowers the member digital product organization in Group Benefits to deliver high-quality member experiences reliably, efficiently and at scale.

Position Responsibilities

Production health, issue management and release excellence

Own the business and product operating approach for digital production health, including issue intake, triage, prioritization, escalation, root-cause analysis and permanent remediation.
Partner with Technology, Operations, Risk and vendors to improve service health, resilience, incident response and the management of member and sponsor irritants and recurring defects.
Lead cross-functional response to significant digital incidents, ensuring timely stakeholder

Digital operations and operating discipline

Own and continuously improve the operating practices required to run Manulife’s Group Benefits member digital channels and capabilities effectively across web, mobile and shared services.
Coordinate operational readiness for material digital changes, ensuring processes, support models, controls, documentation and ownership are in place before launch.

Feature rollout, business readiness and enablement

Lead the end-to-end enablement approach for new digital features and capabilities, from launch, adoption and stabilization.
Partner with Product, Marketing, Communications, Distribution and sponsor-facing teams to create tailored enablement where applicable for plan sponsors, including launch materials, demos, and guidance that help them understand and promote new capabilities.

Strategic initiatives and team leadership

Lead or support selected strategic initiatives as priorities require, particularly those involving complex digital operations, enterprise coordination, rollout or stakeholder adoption.
Provide structured execution leadership for initiatives that span Product, Technology, Operations, Distribution, sponsor-facing teams or enterprise partners.

Required Qualifications

8-10+ years of progressive experience in digital product management, technology delivery, business strategy or transformation, including experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives.
University degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated experience leading the operational readiness, launch and ongoing support of customer-facing digital products or capabilities, including release readiness, production health, issue management and post-launch stabilization.
Proven experience developing and executing business readiness and enablement plans for new capabilities, including stakeholder communications, training, support readiness and adoption.
Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across Product, Technology, Operations and business teams, navigating complex dependencies and competing priorities.
Strong people leadership experience, with a track record of building, coaching and developing high-performing teams.
Strong problem-solving and analytical capability, with experience leading the resolution of complex operational or organizational problems.
Excellent communication, facilitation and stakeholder-management skills, with demonstrated confidence presenting recommendations and complex issues to senior leadership.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

The role being advertised is an existing vacancy.

Manulife Financial Corporation is a leading international financial services provider, helping people make their decisions easier and lives better. To learn more about us, visit https://www.manulife.com/en/about/our-story.html.

Position Purpose

Determines and leads implementation of the University of Ottawa’s digital and web presence strategic vision. Ensures integrated governance of the University’s web ecosystem and optimizes its performance focusing on three areas: content strategy and governance, technology and infrastructure, and user experience. Working closely with information technology leadership, the faculties and the administrative units, ensures that our digital presence supports University priorities and meets the needs of various University clients, in both official languages. Determines directions, standards and practices as a University centre of excellence, ensuring a consistent, accessible and distinctive digital experience. Equips and mobilizes the University web community through guidelines, training, tools and consultations, to increase the quality, consistency and impact of the University’s digital presence. Acts according to the University’s strategic priorities, helping with University promotion and recruitment, as well as quality of services offered to its community. Leads a central team responsible for a diverse portfolio of concurrent, high-visibility web initiatives. Sets priorities, allocates resources wisely and ensures achievement of transformational projects of high value to the University. Ensures links with other marketing and communications office units, including strategic communications, marketing, creative services, public affairs, media relations and language services, to achieve an integrated, consistent and results-based approach.

In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Include

Strategic vision, planning and leadership

Determines and implements the overall uOttawa web presence strategy, in keeping with the leadership focus and uOttawa’s strategic priorities, including with regard to recruitment, promotion and institutional positioning.
Develops and implements the leadership’s multiyear strategic plans and annual workplans, clearly indicating objectives, milestones, deliverables and key performance indicators. Offers clear guidance to the team regarding plan implementation and results measurement.
Determines and documents gaps between university sector operational needs and the state of uOttawa’s web presence, and then plans and achieves required short-, medium- and long-term improvements, working with the affected units.
Innovates by experimenting with and exploiting digital capacities that make work more effective and efficient. Continually monitors emerging trends in design, digital strategy and web technology. Reviews best practices in comparable institutions and recommends changes in strategy to the director.

Web governance and centre of excellence

Establishes, implements and ensures compliance with the web governance framework, including editorial guidelines, quality norms, creation processes, content updates and page lifecycle management. Uses data to build stakeholder consensus and buy-in regarding University directions.
Serves as a strategic consultant to the faculties and administrative units regarding web presence and the digital experience, and turns the digital presence team into a centre of excellence in these areas. Makes guidelines, templates, best practices, training, workshops and tools encouraging consistent adoption of University norms available to the uOttawa web community.
Chairs a web governance committee that includes representatives of communications leadership, IT service leadership, faculties and administrative units to set University priorities, update standards and reconcile competing priorities.
Participates in relevant University committees and working groups dealing with online presence and web governance, and helps with concerted development of concepts and proposals for internal and external audiences.

Information Architecture And User Experience

Supervises design and evolution of information architecture and University website tree structure, based on data and user testing. Guides user experience strategy development for all web properties to ensure accessible, intuitive and efficient navigation for the University’s various audiences.
Supervises user experience audits, usability testing and user research to highlight possible improvements and inform design decisions. Prioritizes interventions based on their measurable impact on recruitment, retention and the University’s profile.

Content and digital visibility strategy

Oversees development and implementation of the University’s web content strategy, including content planning, validation processes and content lifecycle management.
Determines University digital visibility strategy and leads efforts in that regard, both for traditional search engines and emerging tools used for information and comparisons between institutions, such as AI assistants and answer engines. Integrates these technologies with the content strategy to optimize the online experience and discoverability of University content.
Establishes web presence performance indicators — regarding traffic, engagement, conversion and positioning — monitors them and makes data-based recommendations for improvement to the section’s marketing and brand director.

Budget management

Plans and manages the web director’s annual budget according to strategic priorities and resource, technology and training requirements. Determines investment requirements in digital tools and capacity, ensures budget oversight and adjusts plans as needed to control risk.
Supervises and manages relations with vendors, technological partners and external agencies in own area of responsibility. This includes drafting requests for proposals and supervising procurement and project delivery.

Measurability, accountability and continual improvement

Establishes and monitors brand and marketing section performance indicators, regularly checks progress in terms of objectives and expected results, and makes fact-based recommendations to increase productivity and return on investment.
Regularly analyzes web presence results and shares them with section leadership, to support decision making, shape priorities and fuel continual improvement.
Supervises performance audits, surveys on internal partner satisfaction and research needed to inform decisions on digital presence. Uses data and key indicators to guide the team, improve project delivery and optimize resource use.

Team management and talent development

Leads and mobilizes team members, fostering their professional development by encouraging excellence, collaboration and consistency. Provides the necessary support to ensure they make progress and allow them to reach their full potential.
Offers regular feedback, both formal and informal, sets clear performance goals and integrates team activities with other marketing and communications office activities.

Technology and web infrastructure

Oversees web infrastructure to ensure it is sturdy, able to evolve and upgraded (content management, hosting, integration with third-party systems and development projects), working closely with information technology section leadership, within a clear governance framework outlining responsibilities. Ensures that all web properties comply with applicable accessibility standards, including WCAG.

What You Will Bring

Undergraduate degree in digital experience design, communication, digital marketing, computer science or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Master’s an asset.
Ten years’ progressive experience regarding the web and the digital experience, including at least five in a strategic leadership role supervising multidisciplinary teams
Bilingualism – French and English (spoken and written)
In-depth knowledge of digital visibility strategies, including organic SEO and positioning in search engines and generative AI tools, as well as web analytics tools and content management platforms
Hands-on experience in user experience strategy, user research and digital journey optimization
Proven experience in institutional web governance, information architecture and content strategy at scale
Experience in close collaboration with IT teams using a model where content governance and technical infrastructure are managed separately (an asset)
Experience in communication related to organizational transformation projects, with mastery of change management principles
Ability to explain complex technical issues in accessible terms for lay audiences, including decision-makers
Experience in budget management and in handling vendors and technology partners, including drafting requests for proposals and negotiating contracts
Ability to turn institutional web presence priorities into concrete directions and advocate for these directions to senior management
Ability to lead collaboratively and mobilize multidisciplinary teams and internal partners with different interests in a decentralized environment; proven ability to have influence without direct hierarchical authority
Notable ability to manage competing requests and justify own decisions on priorities to senior clients tactfully and firmly
Outstanding ability to co-ordinate multiple files under pressure, establish priorities and meet strict deadlines
Ability to base own action on business results and use data-based strategies to guide decisions, foster consensus and ensure stakeholder buy-in
Ability to work under pressure in a dynamic environment with availability some evenings and weekends as needed
Proven ability to form partnerships and collaborative relationships with diverse internal stakeholders, at different levels of the hierarchy
This position may be subject to a telework agreement.

Key Competencies at uOttawa:

Here are the required competencies for all or our employees at uOttawa:

Planning:
Organize in time a series of actions or events in order to realize an objective or a project. Plan and organize own work and priorities in regular daily activities.

Initiative:
Demonstrate creativity and initiative to suggest improvements and encourage positive results. Is proactive and self-starting. Show availability and willingness to go above and beyond whenever it is possible.

Client Service Orientation:
Help or serve others to meet their needs. This implies anticipating and identifying the needs of internal and external clients and finding solutions on how to meet them.

Teamwork and Cooperation:
Cooperate and work well with other members of the team to reach common goal(s). Accept and give constructive feedback. Able to adjust own behaviour to reach the goals of the team.

The University of Ottawa embraces diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We are passionate about our people and committed to employment equity. We foster a culture of respect, teamwork and inclusion, where collaboration, innovation, and creativity fuel our quest for research and teaching excellence. While all qualified persons are invited to apply, we welcome applications from qualified Indigenous persons, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, women and LGBTQIA2S+ persons. jobs.title: Associate Director, Employee Engagement, Culture and EDI
jobs.description:
Why You’ll Love Working Here

high-performance, people-focused culture
our commitment that equity, diversity, and inclusion are fundamental to our work environment and business success, which helps employees feel valued and empowered to be their authentic selves
learning and development initiatives, including workshops, Speaker Series events and access to LinkedIn Learning, that support employees’ career growth
membership in HOOPP’s world class defined benefit pension plan, which can serve as an important part of your retirement security
competitive, 100% company-paid extended health and dental benefits for permanent employees, including coverage supporting our team's diversity and mental health (e.g., gender affirmation, fertility and drug treatment, psychological support benefits of $2,500 per year, parental leave top-up, and a health spending account).
optional post-retirement health and dental benefits subsidized at 50%
wellness seminars, yoga classes, and free nutritional consultations
the opportunity to make a difference and help take care of those who care for us, by providing a financially secure retirement for Ontario healthcare workers

Job Summary

The Associate Director, Employee Engagement, Culture and EDI leads HOOPP's enterprise approach to employee listening, engagement, culture and inclusion. The role translates employee feedback and workforce insights into clear priorities, equips leaders to take meaningful action and measures.

Working across divisions and in close partnership with Talent, Communications and other enterprise functions, the role advances HOOPP's Culture Principles and EDI commitments through insights, practical programs, governance and accountability. The role reports to the VP, Talent and serves as a trusted adviser to senior leaders on employee sentiment, culture and inclusion.

What You Will Do

Employee listening, insights and action
Own HOOPP's enterprise employee listening strategy, including the annual engagement survey, pulse and lifecycle surveys and other feedback channels, and be accountable for participation, coverage and the quality of listening data
Design survey content, methodology, cadence and benchmarks, and manage survey vendors and platforms in partnership with the HR Enablement team.
Protect respondent confidentiality and anonymity, and set minimum reporting thresholds in line with privacy and information security requirements
Analyze results by division, team, demographic group and employee segment to identify the drivers of engagement and priority gaps
Translate results into clear enterprise and divisional insights, priorities, and recommendations for leaders
Lead the action-planning discipline: coach leaders to translate insights into focused actions, track progress and drive follow-through, assessing whether actions are having the intended impact
Equip people leaders with tools and guidance to interpret and act on feedback
Connect engagement data with other people data, such as turnover, hiring, performance and learning, to give leaders an integrated view of workforce health, working with Talent colleagues
Culture and the Culture Principles
Steward HOOPP's Culture Principles by establishing measures, monitoring progress and identifying opportunities to strengthen how they are lived across HOOPP
Lead culture measurement, including diagnostics and indicators, and report progress against priority engagement and culture indicators, driving focused action where improvement is needed
Partner with the accountable Talent functions to integrate the Culture Principles into hiring, onboarding, performance, recognition and leadership development, which those functions continue to own, and track how fully they are embedded
Advise leaders on the culture implications of organizational change and new ways of working
Equip leaders and managers to model and reinforce the Culture Principles
Support a network of culture champions across divisions
EDI strategy, governance and integration
Lead HOOPP's EDI strategy, roadmap and annual plan
Lead EDI measurement and reporting, including workforce demographic data, representation, employee experience indicators and enterprise scorecards, and report progress against agreed EDI measures
Govern the employee resource group (ERG) program, including charters, executive sponsors, annual plans and measurement of impact
Partner with Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, Talent Management and Learning to integrate inclusion into the people practices they own
Identify inclusion capability needs and partner with L&D and other talent teams to develop appropriate leader and employee supports
Review people policies and practices through an equity lens and recommend changes
Monitor leading practices and external standards, and advise the VP, Talent on implications
Employee experience insights and Improvement
Develop an enterprise view of the employee experience, using employee listening and people data to identify systemic themes, priority moments, and opportunities for improvement across the employee lifecycle
Partner with the accountable Talent and enterprise functions, including Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, Talent Management, Learning, and HR Enablement, to translate employee insights into coordinated improvements, clear ownership and measurable outcomes
Facilitate and track agreed cross-functional improvements, including ownership, commitments and outcomes, and drive closure of systemic employee-experience issues through resolution
Recommend changes to people policies, practices and programs based on insights, recognizing that decisions rest with the accountable owner

Supporting Accountabilities

Communications partnership

Partner with Communications on internal communications about survey launches, results and follow-up, so employees hear what HOOPP heard, what it will do and what has changed
Provide employee insights and culture and EDI content to Communications, which retains accountability for internal and external communications
Review externally shared EDI and culture information for accuracy with Communications and other approvers

Executive advice and reporting

Act as a trusted adviser to the VP, Talent and senior leaders on employee sentiment, culture and inclusion
Prepare executive and Board reporting and insights on engagement, culture and EDI

Program, vendor and budget management

Manage the annual program plan, budget and vendor relationships for the role's programs
Lead cross-divisional working groups and project teams without direct reports
Manage confidential employee data and sensitive matters with discretion

Community impact

Coordinate employee volunteering and giving programs, including participation measurement and employee engagement, in partnership with the functions accountable for sponsorships, external partnerships and reporting

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in business, social sciences, communications or a related field, or equivalent experience; a specific HR credential is not required
7+ years of progressive experience in employee engagement, culture, EDI, organizational effectiveness, HR or related field, including experience leading enterprise-wide programs
Demonstrated experience translating employee and workforce data into insights, recommendations and actions
Experience advising senior executives and influencing without direct authority
Deep expertise in employee engagement, organizational culture and stakeholder management
Strong skills in employee experience, survey design, data analysis, diversity, equity and inclusion, change management, executive communication, program management, influencing and strategic planning
Working knowledge of data privacy, internal communications, vendor management and people analytics; coaching experience is an asset
Brings HOOPP's Culture Principles to life: sets the standard, adapts to win, owns the outcome, decides and drives, says what needs saying and brings out the best

The expected annual base salary range for this role is: $103,000 - $153,000 CAD

The actual base salary offered to the successful candidate may vary based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, individual's expertise and level of experience applicable to the role they are being offered.

This role is eligible to participate in discretionary incentive plan(s), subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan text.

This job is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Sector Director - Infrastructure, Western Canada
jobs.description:
Overview

Colliers Project Leaders is a team committed to projects that make a difference in communities and for the people who live there.

We deliver capital project solutions that strengthen the built environment, partnering with our clients to bring critical infrastructure and complex building projects to life.

We’ve led over 20,000+ projects that:

Make cities more livable
Enhance workplaces
Create spaces people want to return to
Improve patient care
Deliver clean drinking water
Build a sustainable future

And so much more.

This is where you come in. We’re looking for people to join our team who are passionate about creating more sustainable, resilient and inclusive communities.

If this kind of work resonates with you, you’re in the right place

Your role

Lead with purpose. Innovate with impact.

We are seeking a Sector Director to lead growth and strengthen Colliers Project Leaders' position in the Infrastructure sector.

As a Sector Director, you will be accountable for driving sector growth, achieving sales targets, developing strategic client relationships, and building the capabilities needed to expand our market presence. Working across a dynamic matrix organization, you will collaborate with Business Unit leaders, Business Development, Practice Excellence, and practitioners across the business to identify opportunities, lead strategic pursuits, and deliver on our sector growth strategy.

As a recognized leader within your sector, you will develop and execute multi-year growth strategies, manage strategic relationships with new clients, and identify opportunities to integrate our services to address evolving client needs. You will bring a strong understanding of infrastructure market trends, client priorities, procurement environments, and capital project challenges to position Colliers Project Leaders for success.

A key part of your role will be developing our people and strengthening our sector capabilities. You will coach practitioners in consultative sales, account management, and client engagement, while building a network of Infrastructure champions across our Business Units.

A natural collaborator, you thrive in a matrix environment and excel at aligning diverse stakeholders around common goals. You take ownership of organizational priorities and initiatives, translating them into meaningful results across teams and projects. Committed to continuous improvement, you actively seek innovative ways to enhance performance, strengthen operations, and create value for clients.

You will elevate our brand through thought leadership, industry engagement, and impactful client relationships, supported by a strong and growing network across the sector. If you’re ready to influence direction, strengthen market position, and make a visible impact, this is your opportunity to lead and grow at scale.

Responsibilities

Growth & Business Development

Lead the development and execution of the regional Infrastructure sector growth plan, translating market intelligence, client needs, and emerging opportunities into actionable priorities and achieving annual sales targets.
Drive net new business by identifying priority markets, prospective clients, strategic accounts, and opportunities to expand Colliers Project Leaders' presence in the Infrastructure sector, including but not limited to; major projects, transportation, utilities, water and wastewater, energy, and other major capital project markets.
Lead and support pursuits, bringing sector expertise, client insight, and commercial acumen to strengthen our competitive positioning.
Support client discovery, prospecting and competitive pursuits, bringing sector-specific knowledge and relationships to position Colliers Project Leaders for success.
Build and strengthen relationships with key Infrastructure organizations, clients and industry partners.
Understand Infrastructure client buying and procurement behaviours and use those insights to help strengthen our positioning and approach.
Monitor sales pipeline health, maintain accurate and consistent sales information, and support effective opportunity management and forecasting.
Collaborate across regions where opportunities, clients or relationships extend beyond regional boundaries.

Strategy

Direct the development of the Infrastructure sector business plan, with input from key stakeholders, and lead its implementation to achieve annual sector sales targets.
Maintain a strong understanding of trends, challenges and emerging opportunities within the Infrastructure sector and translate those insights into regional growth priorities.
Contribute regional market intelligence and perspective to the broader Infrastructure sector strategy.

Sector Leadership & Capability Development

Demonstrate and act as a role model and influencer of our values.
Serve as an Infrastructure sector resource and advisor to Business Unit leaders, project teams and practitioners, sharing market knowledge and client insight to support growth and delivery.
Coach practitioners and leadership on sales strategies and tactics, develop Infrastructure sector champions within Business Units to expand sector expertise, strengthen client relationships, and build the qualifications and capabilities needed to pursue new opportunities.
Connect project teams, clients and Infrastructure experts across the organization to share knowledge, qualifications and perspectives.
Establish and strengthen Colliers Project Leaders' reputation through thought leadership, industry engagement, conference participation, speaking opportunities, and client engagement.

Management

Lead regional sales planning for Infrastructure, including opportunities to integrate services and capabilities across Colliers Project Leaders.
Clarify and anticipate Infrastructure sector trends, articulate how they affect clients, and develop approaches to capitalize on opportunities or respond to changing market conditions.
Identify the expertise, qualifications and capacity required to pursue and successfully deliver Infrastructure opportunities
Develop Infrastructure sector champions within the Business Units to broaden sector knowledge, relationships and qualifications.
Work with key experts across the organization to build Infrastructure credentials, capability and market profile.

Delivery Excellence, Quality & Risk

Support a culture of quality and consistent adherence to our Sales system and processes.
Drive the integrity, accuracy and consistency of Infrastructure sector and account information to support informed decision-making, pursuit planning and operational excellence.
Identify material delivery, contractual, and commercial risks, provide advice to Business Unit leadership, and escalate significant issues appropriately.
Support teams in understanding client requirements and positioning appropriate commercial terms to protect client outcomes and business interests.

Qualifications

Ten (10) years’ experience as a practitioner (consultant or client side) in the sector is considered an asset. Minimum five (5) years experience in sales is required
Practiced in consultative sales; listening to clients, identifying opportunities, knowing what is required to close the sale, and seeing the sale through
Professional industry credentials relevant and specific to the sector is considered a strong asset
Is a known industry player and leader across the sector regionally and is well connected with key organizations and clients (target and existing) in the sector
An established network of sector contacts regionally and involvement with applicable sector industry and trade associations
Excellent verbal and written communication, facilitation and presentation skills for all levels of our clients and our own organization including a proven ability to write winning proposals
The ability to project and maintain a positive outlook and demonstrate an energetic disposition
Willingness to travel as required locally and within region

Expected Compensation: $126,376 – $173,677 per year (CAD)

This base salary range represents our good faith estimate at the time of posting and is based on market benchmarks and internal equity. The salary offered will be determined based on the successful candidate’s skills, experience, qualifications, and regional consideration. For most new hires, base salary falls between the minimum and the midpoint of the range. While offers above the midpoint are uncommon, they may be considered in exceptional circumstances. This approach helps ensure there is room for future salary growth within the role. In addition to base salary, the total rewards package may include annual bonus opportunities, employer RRSP contributions, comprehensive group benefits, including a Health Care Spending Account, and other benefits.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Don’t have every single qualification?
We know that some people are less likely to apply for a job unless they are a perfect match. At Colliers Project Leaders, we’re not looking for “perfect matches.” We’re looking to welcome people to our diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you’re excited about this role but don’t have every single qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. Whether it’s this role or another one, you may be just the right candidate.

What You Can Expect

An opportunity to truly impact our communities
A flexible work environment
A comprehensive onboarding experience
Significant professional development, training, and a mentorship program
A paid volunteer day
An environment where people feel welcome, heard and included, regardless of their differences
And much more!

Join our team of difference-makers and help shape the growth of dynamic communities.

Disclaimer

Colliers Project Leaders is part of Colliers (NASDAQ, TSX: CIGI), a leading diversified professional services and investment management company, with more than 18,000 professionals operating in 63 countries.

We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from all qualified individuals. If you require accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact the assigned Talent Acquisition Business Partner.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use

We may use technology tools to assist in screening applications for keywords or qualifications. However, final selection decisions are made by our hiring team through human review and interviews.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis. The employer will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Makes guidelines, templates, best practices, training, workshops and tools encouraging consistent adoption of University norms available to the uOttawa web community.
Chairs a web governance committee that includes representatives of communications leadership, IT service leadership, faculties and administrative units to set University priorities, update standards and reconcile competing priorities.
Participates in relevant University committees and working groups dealing with online presence and web governance, and helps with concerted development of concepts and proposals for internal and external audiences.

Information Architecture And User Experience

Supervises design and evolution of information architecture and University website tree structure, based on data and user testing. Guides user experience strategy development for all web properties to ensure accessible, intuitive and efficient navigation for the University’s various audiences.
Supervises user experience audits, usability testing and user research to highlight possible improvements and inform design decisions. Prioritizes interventions based on their measurable impact on recruitment, retention and the University’s profile.

Content and digital visibility strategy

Oversees development and implementation of the University’s web content strategy, including content planning, validation processes and content lifecycle management.
Determines University digital visibility strategy and leads efforts in that regard, both for traditional search engines and emerging tools used for information and comparisons between institutions, such as AI assistants and answer engines. Integrates these technologies with the content strategy to optimize the online experience and discoverability of University content.
Establishes web presence performance indicators — regarding traffic, engagement, conversion and positioning — monitors them and makes data-based recommendations for improvement to the section’s marketing and brand director.

Budget management

Plans and manages the web director’s annual budget according to strategic priorities and resource, technology and training requirements. Determines investment requirements in digital tools and capacity, ensures budget oversight and adjusts plans as needed to control risk.
Supervises and manages relations with vendors, technological partners and external agencies in own area of responsibility. This includes drafting requests for proposals and supervising procurement and project delivery.

Measurability, accountability and continual improvement

Establishes and monitors brand and marketing section performance indicators, regularly checks progress in terms of objectives and expected results, and makes fact-based recommendations to increase productivity and return on investment.
Regularly analyzes web presence results and shares them with section leadership, to support decision making, shape priorities and fuel continual improvement.
Supervises performance audits, surveys on internal partner satisfaction and research needed to inform decisions on digital presence. Uses data and key indicators to guide the team, improve project delivery and optimize resource use.

Team management and talent development

Leads and mobilizes team members, fostering their professional development by encouraging excellence, collaboration and consistency. Provides the necessary support to ensure they make progress and allow them to reach their full potential.
Offers regular feedback, both formal and informal, sets clear performance goals and integrates team activities with other marketing and communications office activities.

Technology and web infrastructure

Oversees web infrastructure to ensure it is sturdy, able to evolve and upgraded (content management, hosting, integration with third-party systems and development projects), working closely with information technology section leadership, within a clear governance framework outlining responsibilities. Ensures that all web properties comply with applicable accessibility standards, including WCAG.

What You Will Bring

Undergraduate degree in digital experience design, communication, digital marketing, computer science or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Master’s an asset.
Ten years’ progressive experience regarding the web and the digital experience, including at least five in a strategic leadership role supervising multidisciplinary teams
Bilingualism – French and English (spoken and written)
In-depth knowledge of digital visibility strategies, including organic SEO and positioning in search engines and generative AI tools, as well as web analytics tools and content management platforms
Hands-on experience in user experience strategy, user research and digital journey optimization
Proven experience in institutional web governance, information architecture and content strategy at scale
Experience in close collaboration with IT teams using a model where content governance and technical infrastructure are managed separately (an asset)
Experience in communication related to organizational transformation projects, with mastery of change management principles
Ability to explain complex technical issues in accessible terms for lay audiences, including decision-makers
Experience in budget management and in handling vendors and technology partners, including drafting requests for proposals and negotiating contracts
Ability to turn institutional web presence priorities into concrete directions and advocate for these directions to senior management
Ability to lead collaboratively and mobilize multidisciplinary teams and internal partners with different interests in a decentralized environment; proven ability to have influence without direct hierarchical authority
Notable ability to manage competing requests and justify own decisions on priorities to senior clients tactfully and firmly
Outstanding ability to co-ordinate multiple files under pressure, establish priorities and meet strict deadlines
Ability to base own action on business results and use data-based strategies to guide decisions, foster consensus and ensure stakeholder buy-in
Ability to work under pressure in a dynamic environment with availability some evenings and weekends as needed
Proven ability to form partnerships and collaborative relationships with diverse internal stakeholders, at different levels of the hierarchy
This position may be subject to a telework agreement.

Key Competencies at uOttawa:

Here are the required competencies for all or our employees at uOttawa:

Planning:
Organize in time a series of actions or events in order to realize an objective or a project. Plan and organize own work and priorities in regular daily activities.

Initiative:
Demonstrate creativity and initiative to suggest improvements and encourage positive results. Is proactive and self-starting. Show availability and willingness to go above and beyond whenever it is possible.

Client Service Orientation:
Help or serve others to meet their needs. This implies anticipating and identifying the needs of internal and external clients and finding solutions on how to meet them.

Teamwork and Cooperation:
Cooperate and work well with other members of the team to reach common goal(s). Accept and give constructive feedback. Able to adjust own behaviour to reach the goals of the team.

new_jobs.title: Associate Director, Employee Engagement, Culture and EDI
new_jobs.description:
Why You’ll Love Working Here

high-performance, people-focused culture
our commitment that equity, diversity, and inclusion are fundamental to our work environment and business success, which helps employees feel valued and empowered to be their authentic selves
learning and development initiatives, including workshops, Speaker Series events and access to LinkedIn Learning, that support employees’ career growth
membership in HOOPP’s world class defined benefit pension plan, which can serve as an important part of your retirement security
competitive, 100% company-paid extended health and dental benefits for permanent employees, including coverage supporting our team's diversity and mental health (e.g., gender affirmation, fertility and drug treatment, psychological support benefits of $2,500 per year, parental leave top-up, and a health spending account).
optional post-retirement health and dental benefits subsidized at 50%
wellness seminars, yoga classes, and free nutritional consultations
the opportunity to make a difference and help take care of those who care for us, by providing a financially secure retirement for Ontario healthcare workers

Job Summary

The Associate Director, Employee Engagement, Culture and EDI leads HOOPP's enterprise approach to employee listening, engagement, culture and inclusion. The role translates employee feedback and workforce insights into clear priorities, equips leaders to take meaningful action and measures.

Working across divisions and in close partnership with Talent, Communications and other enterprise functions, the role advances HOOPP's Culture Principles and EDI commitments through insights, practical programs, governance and accountability. The role reports to the VP, Talent and serves as a trusted adviser to senior leaders on employee sentiment, culture and inclusion.

What You Will Do

Employee listening, insights and action
Own HOOPP's enterprise employee listening strategy, including the annual engagement survey, pulse and lifecycle surveys and other feedback channels, and be accountable for participation, coverage and the quality of listening data
Design survey content, methodology, cadence and benchmarks, and manage survey vendors and platforms in partnership with the HR Enablement team.
Protect respondent confidentiality and anonymity, and set minimum reporting thresholds in line with privacy and information security requirements
Analyze results by division, team, demographic group and employee segment to identify the drivers of engagement and priority gaps
Translate results into clear enterprise and divisional insights, priorities, and recommendations for leaders
Lead the action-planning discipline: coach leaders to translate insights into focused actions, track progress and drive follow-through, assessing whether actions are having the intended impact
Equip people leaders with tools and guidance to interpret and act on feedback
Connect engagement data with other people data, such as turnover, hiring, performance and learning, to give leaders an integrated view of workforce health, working with Talent colleagues
Culture and the Culture Principles
Steward HOOPP's Culture Principles by establishing measures, monitoring progress and identifying opportunities to strengthen how they are lived across HOOPP
Lead culture measurement, including diagnostics and indicators, and report progress against priority engagement and culture indicators, driving focused action where improvement is needed
Partner with the accountable Talent functions to integrate the Culture Principles into hiring, onboarding, performance, recognition and leadership development, which those functions continue to own, and track how fully they are embedded
Advise leaders on the culture implications of organizational change and new ways of working
Equip leaders and managers to model and reinforce the Culture Principles
Support a network of culture champions across divisions
EDI strategy, governance and integration
Lead HOOPP's EDI strategy, roadmap and annual plan
Lead EDI measurement and reporting, including workforce demographic data, representation, employee experience indicators and enterprise scorecards, and report progress against agreed EDI measures
Govern the employee resource group (ERG) program, including charters, executive sponsors, annual plans and measurement of impact
Partner with Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, Talent Management and Learning to integrate inclusion into the people practices they own
Identify inclusion capability needs and partner with L&D and other talent teams to develop appropriate leader and employee supports
Review people policies and practices through an equity lens and recommend changes
Monitor leading practices and external standards, and advise the VP, Talent on implications
Employee experience insights and Improvement
Develop an enterprise view of the employee experience, using employee listening and people data to identify systemic themes, priority moments, and opportunities for improvement across the employee lifecycle
Partner with the accountable Talent and enterprise functions, including Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, Talent Management, Learning, and HR Enablement, to translate employee insights into coordinated improvements, clear ownership and measurable outcomes
Facilitate and track agreed cross-functional improvements, including ownership, commitments and outcomes, and drive closure of systemic employee-experience issues through resolution
Recommend changes to people policies, practices and programs based on insights, recognizing that decisions rest with the accountable owner

Supporting Accountabilities

Communications partnership

Partner with Communications on internal communications about survey launches, results and follow-up, so employees hear what HOOPP heard, what it will do and what has changed
Provide employee insights and culture and EDI content to Communications, which retains accountability for internal and external communications
Review externally shared EDI and culture information for accuracy with Communications and other approvers

Executive advice and reporting

Act as a trusted adviser to the VP, Talent and senior leaders on employee sentiment, culture and inclusion
Prepare executive and Board reporting and insights on engagement, culture and EDI

Program, vendor and budget management

Manage the annual program plan, budget and vendor relationships for the role's programs
Lead cross-divisional working groups and project teams without direct reports
Manage confidential employee data and sensitive matters with discretion

Community impact

Coordinate employee volunteering and giving programs, including participation measurement and employee engagement, in partnership with the functions accountable for sponsorships, external partnerships and reporting

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in business, social sciences, communications or a related field, or equivalent experience; a specific HR credential is not required
7+ years of progressive experience in employee engagement, culture, EDI, organizational effectiveness, HR or related field, including experience leading enterprise-wide programs
Demonstrated experience translating employee and workforce data into insights, recommendations and actions
Experience advising senior executives and influencing without direct authority
Deep expertise in employee engagement, organizational culture and stakeholder management
Strong skills in employee experience, survey design, data analysis, diversity, equity and inclusion, change management, executive communication, program management, influencing and strategic planning
Working knowledge of data privacy, internal communications, vendor management and people analytics; coaching experience is an asset
Brings HOOPP's Culture Principles to life: sets the standard, adapts to win, owns the outcome, decides and drives, says what needs saying and brings out the best

The expected annual base salary range for this role is: $103,000 - $153,000 CAD

The actual base salary offered to the successful candidate may vary based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, individual's expertise and level of experience applicable to the role they are being offered.

This role is eligible to participate in discretionary incentive plan(s), subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan text.

This job is for an existing vacancy.

HOOPP may use artificial intelligence tools to assist in screening, assessing and selecting applicants for this position. These tools support our recruitment process but do not replace human judgment and decision-making.
